data.name: Adom
data.gender_notes: Adom is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word 'adamah' meaning 'red earth'. In Genesis, God formed man from the earth and named him Adam. The name Adom carries the meaning “First man” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Adom usually hope their child will grow to embody first man and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of God's creation and mankind's connection to the earth.
data.etymology: Adom belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “First man.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adom total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_hebrew.name: אדום
in_hebrew.meaning: אדום: האדמה, ארץ, אדום, מלכות אדום
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אדום הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אדמה' או 'ארץ'. הוא קשור קשר הדוק לאדמה ולטבע. באתר המקרא, השם אדום מתייחס לאזור שממזרח לישראל, הידוע גם כארץ אדום. שם זה גם מתקשר למלכות אדום, אחת ממלכויות האזור בימי קדם.

in_greek.name: Άδων
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Άδων είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος 'אדום' (Adom). Στην ελληνική παράδοση, το όνομα συνδέεται με την έννοια του 'παραδείσου' ή 'κήπου του Θεού'. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, παρόλο που δεν αναφέρεται άμεσα, η έννοια της γης και της δημιουργίας είναι κεντρική στη διδασκαλία του Χριστού.

in_latin.name: Adom
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Adom derivatur ex hebraico 'אדום' (Adom), quod significat 'terra' vel 'solum'. In traditione christiana, nomen Adom refert ad creationem et originem mundi. Est nomen quod connexionem cum natura et terra habet.

in_english.name: Adom
in_english.long_meaning: The name Adom originates from the Hebrew 'אדום' (Adom), meaning 'earth' or 'ground'. It is associated with the biblical land of Edom, east of Israel. In Christian tradition, Adom symbolizes the connection to the earth and nature. The name implies a strong bond with the land and creation.

data.cultural_impact: The name Adom has Semitic origins, specifically from the Hebrew language, and is considered a biblical name. It holds cultural significance in Judeo-Christian traditions. In mythology, Adam is the first man created by God, spoken of as the protogonos or "primeval being". His creation signifies the beginning of the human race.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Adom holds deep spiritual significance as it symbolizes humanity's creation from the earth and God's active role in shaping and giving life to all people. It serves as a reminder of our connection to the natural world and our Creator, who imbued within us the divine spark of life. Additionally, in Christian belief, the name Adam is connected to the promise of the restoration of humanity through Christ's redeeming work. Consequently, the name Adom carries themes of creation, connection, and redemption.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Adom, meaning “earth” or “man” in Hebrew, symbolizes our connection to the soil from which we were created and the inherent dignity bestowed upon us as God's image-bearers. It is a reminder of our rootedness in the divine plan and the stewardship of the Earth we have been entrusted with.

biblical_reference.note: The name Adom (Edom) is mentioned in the context of Esau, who sold his birthright to Jacob for a bowl of red stew, hence named Edom (Adom) because of the red color.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In ancient Christian tradition, Adom was a revered saint. The name Adom carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Adom was popularized by a 5th-century saint who was known for his piety and charitable works.

trends: use in fiction as a character name
modern_usage.modern_context: The name Adom remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Elizabeth Adom from Athens, Greece embodies the meaning of Adom - "First man". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.
